Query: we are a 50-person SaaS company with many women employees, we collect user data and bill overseas clients — what are all our compliance obligations
Valid as of: 2026-10-15

SUMMARY
- Corporate Governance: Corporate governance for a 50-person company involves mandatory board composition, director appointment procedures, and strict financial reporting and disclosure obligations.
- Corporate Governance (not addressed by retrieved provisions): The provisions do not provide specific governance requirements based on the headcount of 50 employees; the obligations listed apply based on the company's status as a private or public company.
- Data Protection: SaaS companies must obtain informed, specific consent for data processing and maintain reasonable security safeguards.
- Data Protection: Companies must provide clear notices, manage data breaches, and honor Data Principal rights regarding data access and erasure.
- Data Protection: some of these obligations are not yet in force on 2026-10-15; each step below shows the date it applies from.
- Data Protection (not addressed by retrieved provisions): The provided provisions do not address specific compliance requirements for different company sizes (e.g., small vs. large startups) other than the 'Significant Data Fiduciary' designation, nor do they provide specific guidance for employee-type data beyond general legitimate use categories.
- Intellectual Property: SaaS companies must manage copyright ownership for software code and register trademarks to protect their brand identity.
- Intellectual Property: Assignments of intellectual property must be executed in writing with specific terms regarding duration and scope.
- Intellectual Property (not addressed by retrieved provisions): Specific procedural forms for trademark applications and detailed litigation processes for copyright infringement beyond assignment disputes.
- Taxation & GST: SaaS exports are classified as zero-rated inter-State supplies, allowing for tax-free exports under bond or LUT.
- Taxation & GST: Compliance involves specific invoicing, reporting, and refund procedures for unutilised input tax credits.
- Taxation & GST (not addressed by retrieved provisions): The provided provisions do not cover specific income tax filing requirements for the startup's corporate entity or specific GST registration thresholds.
- Employment & Workplace: Compliance obligations for a 50-person startup include establishing an Internal Complaints Committee for sexual harassment, ensuring equal pay and non-discrimination in employment, and providing maternity benefits.
- Employment & Workplace: Employers must also adhere to specific safety and search protocols for women employees.

ACTION CHECKLIST
**Corporate Governance**
Step 1: Ensure the company has at least two directors, with at least one director residing in India for 182 days or more during the financial year. — [ca_2013_sec_149] (applies to: private) [NOTE: only partly supported by the cited text]
Step 2: Ensure directors are appointed by the company in a general meeting, possess a Director Identification Number, and file their consent to act as a director with the Registrar within thirty days of appointment. — [ca_2013_sec_152] (applies to: both)
Step 3: The Board of Directors must approve and sign the financial statements, and include a Board's report containing a Directors' Responsibility Statement and details on frauds, loans, and related party contracts. — [ca_2013_sec_134] (applies to: both)
Step 4: Send copies of audited financial statements and the auditor's report to every member at least twenty-one days before the general meeting. — [ca_2013_sec_136] (applies to: both)
Step 5: If a body corporate is a member, it may authorize a representative via a Board resolution to exercise rights and powers, including voting, at company meetings. — [ca_2013_sec_113] (applies to: both)
Step 6: If appointing an independent director, the company may select them from a notified data bank, and the appointment must be approved by the company in a general meeting. — [ca_2013_sec_150] (applies to: both)

**Data Protection**
Step 7: Ensure all data processing is for a lawful purpose and based on valid consent or legitimate uses. — [dpdp_act_2023_sec_4] [NOTE: Not yet in force on 2026-10-15; applies from 2027-05-13.]
Step 8: Provide a notice to the Data Principal before or at the time of requesting consent, detailing the data collected, purpose, and rights. — [dpdp_act_2023_sec_5] [NOTE: Not yet in force on 2026-10-15; applies from 2027-05-13.]
Step 9: Ensure the notice is understandable independently, uses clear language, includes an itemized description of data, and provides links to exercise rights or make complaints. — [dpdp_rules_2025_sec_3] [NOTE: Not yet in force on 2026-10-15; applies from 2027-05-13.]
Step 10: Obtain free, specific, informed, and unambiguous consent; allow withdrawal of consent with the same ease as it was given. — [dpdp_act_2023_sec_6] [NOTE: only partly supported by the cited text] [NOTE: Not yet in force on 2026-10-15; applies from 2027-05-13.]
Step 11: Comply with general obligations including appointing Data Processors only via valid contract, implementing security safeguards, and establishing a grievance redressal mechanism. — [dpdp_act_2023_sec_8] [NOTE: Not yet in force on 2026-10-15; applies from 2027-05-13.]
Step 12: Obtain verifiable parental/guardian consent before processing data of children or persons with disabilities; avoid detrimental processing, tracking, or targeted advertising for children. — [dpdp_act_2023_sec_9] [NOTE: Not yet in force on 2026-10-15; applies from 2027-05-13.]
Step 13: If notified as a Significant Data Fiduciary, appoint a Data Protection Officer based in India, an independent data auditor, and conduct periodic Data Protection Impact Assessments. — [dpdp_act_2023_sec_10] [NOTE: Not yet in force on 2026-10-15; applies from 2027-05-13.]
Step 14: Provide Data Principals with a summary of their processed personal data and the identities of other Fiduciaries or Processors with whom data has been shared. — [dpdp_act_2023_sec_11] [NOTE: Not yet in force on 2026-10-15; applies from 2027-05-13.]
Step 15: Intimate the Board and affected Data Principals of any personal data breach in the prescribed manner, including details of the breach and mitigation measures. — [dpdp_rules_2025_sec_7] [NOTE: only partly supported by the cited text] [NOTE: Not yet in force on 2026-10-15; applies from 2027-05-13.]
Step 16: Publish business contact information for the Data Protection Officer or a designated person to answer Data Principal queries on your website or app. — [dpdp_rules_2025_sec_9] [NOTE: Not yet in force on 2026-10-15; applies from 2027-05-13.]

**Intellectual Property**
Step 17: Recognize that computer programs are classified as 'literary works' under copyright law. — [copyright_act_1957_sec_2]
Step 18: Exercise exclusive rights to reproduce, sell, or rent computer programs, including storing them in electronic media. — [copyright_act_1957_sec_14]
Step 19: Ensure employment contracts specify copyright ownership, as the employer is the default first owner for works created during employment unless otherwise agreed. — [copyright_act_1957_sec_17] [NOTE: only partly supported by the cited text]
Step 20: Assign copyright in existing or future works, noting that assignments for future works only take effect upon creation and cannot apply to media not in commercial use at the time of assignment. — [copyright_act_1957_sec_18]
Step 21: Execute all copyright assignments in writing, identifying the work, rights, duration, and territory; defaults are 5 years and India-wide if not specified. — [copyright_act_1957_sec_19]
Step 22: Apply in writing to the Registrar to register trademarks for goods or services, noting that the Registrar may accept or refuse the application. — [trademarks_act_1999_sec_18]
Step 23: Register third parties as 'registered users' of a trademark, which allows their use to be legally attributed to the proprietor. — [trademarks_act_1999_sec_48]

**Taxation & GST**
Step 24: Classify the supply of SaaS to overseas clients as an 'inter-State supply' where the supplier is in India and the recipient is outside India. — [igst_act_2017_sec_7] (applies to: both)
Step 25: Treat the export of services as a 'zero rated supply', which allows for the availment of input tax credit even if the supply is exempt. — [igst_act_2017_sec_16] (applies to: both) [NOTE: only partly supported by the cited text]
Step 26: Furnish a bond or Letter of Undertaking (LUT) in FORM GST RFD-11 prior to export if opting to supply services without payment of integrated tax. — [cgst_rules_2017_rule_96a] (applies to: both)
Step 27: Determine the place of supply for online information and database access or retrieval services based on the location of the recipient, verified by specific indicators like billing address or IP address. — [igst_act_2017_sec_13] (applies to: both) [NOTE: only partly supported by the cited text]

**Employment & Workplace**
Step 28: Constitute an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) via written order at every office or unit, ensuring it is chaired by a senior-level woman employee, includes an NGO member, and has at least 50% women members. — [posh_2013_sec_4] (applies to: both) [NOTE: only partly supported by the cited text]
Step 29: Prohibit sexual harassment at the workplace, including quid pro quo scenarios and the creation of a hostile work environment. — [posh_2013_sec_3] (applies to: both)
Step 30: Accept written complaints of sexual harassment from aggrieved women (or their legal heirs if incapacitated) within three months of the incident, and assist the complainant in drafting the complaint if necessary. — [posh_2013_sec_9] (applies to: both)
Step 31: Pay equal remuneration to men and women for the same or similar work; you cannot reduce the pay of one sex to achieve equality. — [era_1976_sec_4] (applies to: both)
Step 32: Ensure no discrimination against women in recruitment, promotion, training, or transfer, unless legally restricted. — [era_1976_sec_5] (applies to: both)
Step 33: Permit the employment of women for all types of work, including before 6 a.m. and after 7 p.m., provided they consent and safety/working-hour conditions are met. — [oshwc_2020_sec_43] (applies to: both)
Step 34: Provide maternity benefits (paid leave) to eligible women who have worked for at least 80 days in the preceding 12 months, for a maximum of 26 weeks (or 12 weeks for women with two or more surviving children or adopting mothers). — [mba_1961_sec_5] (applies to: both) [NOTE: only partly supported by the cited text]
Step 35: Ensure that if a search of a woman employee is required, it is conducted only by another woman. — [ieso_rules_1946_IA_21] (applies to: both)

**Corporate Governance**
Step 1: Appoint at least two directors for a private company, ensuring at least one director stays in India for at least 182 days during the financial year. — [ca_2013_sec_149] (applies to: private) [NOTE: only partly supported by the cited text]
Step 2: Ensure all directors have a Director Identification Number (DIN) and file their consent to act as a director with the Registrar within 30 days of appointment. — [ca_2013_sec_152] (applies to: both) [NOTE: only partly supported by the cited text]
